transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-22
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 55m
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Veridian Head of Search), Daniel Kim (ML Engineer), Liam O'Neill (Infra)

Summary:
Quick discovery to understand Veridian's embedding pipeline, tolerance for latency vs unit cost, and constraints for integrating with their in-house vector store. Looking to decide between Redwood Hosted / Dedicated / Private for an initial rerank + hybrid search pilot. Customer cares about throughput during peak 200 qps, tail latency 95th < 150ms for first-pass, rerank < 600ms for end-to-end, and data residency (EU). They are testing 512 and 1024 dim models and curious about quantization tradeoffs.

Topics:
- current embedding generator (open-source gpt-embedding-3b fork) -> 512 dims, in-house quantized ONNX
- vector DB: self-hosted Milvus cluster (sharded across 3 regions) + online feature store
- traffic pattern: diurnal peaks to 200 qps, long tail of small spikes, 120M active docs
- success criteria: precision@10 for rerank >= 0.78, cost per 1M queries within budget
- hosting options: host vs dedicated vs private VPC

Transcript body (timestamps approximate):
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, can you quick intro who you are
[00:03] Marta Ruiz: yeah I'm Marta, head of search at Veridian, I run the search infra and ranking team
[00:07] Daniel Kim: daniel, i own embeddings and the pipeline, we run an off-the-shelf embedder then do rerank with a 7B model
[00:11] Priya Nair: priya from redwood, i'll focus on perf details and benchmarks
[00:13] Liam O'Neill: liam infra, i manage our milvus cluster and cloud accounts
[00:16] Alex Chen: perfect thanks. big picture what problem are you trying to solve with embeddings + rerank
[00:25] Marta: we want to improve product search relevance, especially long tail queries and multi-intent queries, current recall okay but rerank improves precision
[00:30] Daniel: we have 120m docs, embeddings at 512 dims, currently faiss flat indexes, but we hit latency spikes when fanout > 32
[00:40] Priya: got it, and what are your latency goals and throughput? any SLOs?
[00:44] Marta: 95th for first-pass < 150ms, rerank end-to-end < 600ms. peak qps about 200, sustained ~80
[00:51] Alex: are you flexible on dims? any experiments with 768? 1024?
[00:55] Daniel: we've tried 768 on a small shard, accuracy up ~1.8%, but cost and vector size worried us; disk and memory growth was painful
[01:05] Priya: ok, so common patterns: higher dims help recall but increase I/O/throughput burden. We recommend 512 for high-throughput first-pass then 1024 (or 7b reranker) for rerank. Also quantized embeddings (8-bit/4-bit) can halve memory but may affect similarity quality depending on model.
[01:20] Liam: another constraint: data residency EU — can you support regionally isolated hosting? we also have strict audit logs and SSO
[01:28] Alex: yes, Redwood Private supports EU-only control plane + VPC, Dedicated can be provisioned in eu-west, Hosted has EU regions if you need quick start but data egress rules differ
[01:40] Marta: security is big; we need SOC 2 type II and packet capture for debugging. also KMS for key management
[01:48] Priya: we have SOC2, supports customer-managed KMS for Private/Dedicated, audit logs available in Console (can push to your SIEM)
[01:55] Daniel: curious about integration with Milvus: do you recommend moving index into Redwood Dedicated or keep Milvus and call Redwood for embeddings and rerank?
[02:05] Priya: two patterns: 1) keep Milvus for vector search (we return embeddings or vectors and you do search) or 2) we host a fast ANN layer as part of Redwood Dedicated and provide fallback to your Milvus. Hybrid search uses cached prefixes and rerank model in our runtime — reduces tail latency. For throughput, Dedicated lets you reserve GPU pools for steady qps to meet 95th targets.
[02:28] Liam: if we keep Milvus, how does batching and KV cache work across network boundary? i worry about network hops
[02:34] Priya: good question — batching happens at our runtime; if Milvus is external we recommend colocating an edge replica to reduce RTT. Redwood's prefix/KV cache can store vectors for hot docs to avoid repeated Milvus calls.
[02:48] Daniel: what about embedding dimension mismatch? our store currently 512, if rerank uses 1024 embeddings, how do we reconcile?
[02:56] Priya: two approaches — store both 512 and 1024 vectors (double storage) or use a mapping model to project 1024->512 for ANN, then rerank with full model. Many customers opt for 512 first-pass and compute on-the-fly 1024 for the top-K.
[03:10] Marta: performance numbers — can we get sample latencies for 512 first-pass at 200 qps and rerank 7b for top 20?
[03:18] Priya: i'll share benchmark sheet; rough expectation: dedicated GPU pool with batching can get <120ms 95th for 512 first-pass at 200 qps; rerank 7b for 20 items with optimized kernels ~350–550ms depending on quantization and sequence length
[03:35] Alex: cost question — what's the unit math for 1M queries with fanout 20 + rerank for top10?
[03:41] Priya: we'll model it — depends on batch efficiency, quantization and whether you're on Hosted or Dedicated. i'll prepare cost scenarios with your qps and retention needs
[03:48] Daniel: we also need determinism for evals — can you pin model versions and capture outputs for A/B?
[03:53] Priya: yes, rollout and version pinning in Console, stored evals and regression alerts tied to prompt sets
[04:00] Marta: any competitors or pitfalls we should watch for?
[04:03] Alex: some customers evaluated pinecone for simple ANN but needed more control for rerank; others ran into throughput limits on managed ANN when fanout high
[04:10] Liam: wondered about disaster recovery for Private deployment
[04:14] Priya: Private supports multi-region replicas and we can assist with runbook; DR depends on your RTO/RPO requirements
[04:22] Marta: ok next steps: we'll send sample logs and share a short list of queries. we'll reconvene after we see your benchmarks
[04:30] Alex: great — to recap we'll send: tailored cost+throughput model, benchmark links for dims/quantization, and a checklist for log export. priya will run the 512/768/1024 evals and share numbers.
[04:45] Daniel: thanks all, good convo
[04:47] Marta: thanks

End of transcript.
